characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: X-Pert PRO diffractometer with Cu-Kα radiation; scan 2θ 40°–120°, step size 0.03°; only the (110) peak used for dislocation density determination (Variance method of Wilson and Groma, Eq. 7 and Eq. 8); dislocation contrast factor from ANIZC; Si standard for instrumental broadening
characterization_methods.key_findings: For the 98%CR Fe-6.8Al sample: crystallite size 102.3 ± 9.8 nm; lattice micro-strain 1.46 × 10^-3; dislocation density ~2.2 × 10^15 m^-2; the (110) peak of the 98%CR sample is strongly broadened (dominantly from lattice micro-strain/dislocations) relative to the annealed samples.
characterization_methods.purpose: determination of dislocation density, crystallite size and lattice micro-strain of the ferrite matrix

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: FEI-ESEM Quanta 200 at 25 kV accelerating voltage
characterization_methods.key_findings: The 98% cold rolled sample shows heavily elongated and pancaked grains along the rolling directions with shear bands at ~40° to RD indicating non-uniform deformation; the average width of the deformed lamellae is 2.6 ± 1.2 μm.
characterization_methods.purpose: microstructural investigation of the Fe-6.8Al sample in the cold rolled condition

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: TEM sample prepared by grinding and twin-jet electropolishing in a solution of 78% methanol, 10% lactic acid, 7% sulfuric acid, 3% nitric acid and 2% hydrochloric acid
characterization_methods.key_findings: SAED from the [011] zone axis shows strong matrix spots plus weak superlattice spots from the ordered phase; the dark-field image (from the weak 001-type spots) shows very fine ordered phase (bright) against a dark background with a size of 2.1 ± 0.2 nm, in correlation with SAXS.
characterization_methods.purpose: detection of the ordered phase in the Fe-6.8Al sample
characterization_methods.technique: Transmission Electron Microscopy (dark-field imaging and selected-area electron diffraction, SAED)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: conventional constant acceleration Doppler velocity drive with 57Co (Rh-matrix) source, transmission geometry; velocity calibrated with pure α-Fe foil; spectra fitted by the NORMOS program (up to 40 sextets); powder samples wrapped in Cu foil, sealed in a glass tube under high vacuum (10^-5 mBar) and annealed at 600 °C for 60 min
characterization_methods.key_findings: The Fe-6.8Al B_hf distribution is a broad hump deconvoluted into five components (B_hf = 32.68, 30.34, 27.69, 25.05 and 23.26 T); the 30.34 T component dominates (Area ≈ 45.45%, V_f ≈ 44%); a low-intensity ~23 T component (V_f ≈ 1.4%) indicates a low volume fraction of the Fe3Al ordered phase.
characterization_methods.purpose: examination of the local atomic configuration and formation of ordered phase in the Fe-Al low-density steels

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: laboratory-based dual energy Mo-Cr-SAXS system (Xeuss, Xenocs, France); camera lengths 550 and 2400 mm; q-range 0.0254 to 10 nm^-1; FIT2D for azimuthal integration; glassy carbon secondary standard; Silver-Behenate for scattering-angle calibration; samples sandwiched between Scotch Magic tape
characterization_methods.key_findings: Scattering from the nano-sized ordered phase appears as a weak peak between q = 0.3–3 nm^-1 with a q^-4 decay below 0.3 nm^-1 from larger heterogeneities (grains/grain boundaries); the Fe3Al ordered-phase diameter increases from 2.5 ± 0.15 nm to 3.75 ± 0.2 nm with increasing Al content (5 to 9 wt%).
characterization_methods.purpose: quantitative estimation of size, volume fraction and number density of the nano-sized ordered Fe3Al phase

analytical_models.equation_role: tau_ss = G * eps_s^(3/2) * c^(1/2) / 700, with eps_s = |eps_G' - beta*eps_b|
analytical_models.model_note: Value of tau_ss = 95.6 MPa calculated for the Fe-6.8Al alloy; solid-solution strengthening for Fe-Al rises from 67.8 to 127.2 MPa for 5 to 9 wt% Al.
Eq. (10) gives tau_PN at 0 K; due to thermal energy a lower value of 41 MPa (from Speich and Swann for 0.4 wt% C-steel) was used at room temperature owing to lack of Fe-Al data.
Ordered-phase size determined by both TEM and SAXS in this study.
k_HP for 99.95% pure iron (Refs. [49,50]) used; ferrite grain/crystallite size determined by SEM for annealed and by XRD for cold rolled samples.

analytical_models.equation_role: delta_sigma_rho = M * alpha * G * b * rho^(1/2)
analytical_models.model_note: Dislocation density determined by the variance method applied to the (110) XRD peak profile.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Applied to the Fe-6.8Al alloy in the 98%CR and annealed (750 °C, 5 and 60 min) conditions; dislocation density and grain/crystallite size taken from XRD/SEM of the respective conditions.
computational_details.simulation_method: Analytical modeling of the yield strength by superposition of five strengthening mechanisms (dislocations, grain size, ordered phase, solid solution and lattice frictional stress) applied to the Fe-6.8Al samples.
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: For the 98%CR sample the modeled contributions sum to the measured YS = 1800 MPa; strengthening from dislocations (generated during rolling) and grain boundaries are identified as the two dominant mechanisms.

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: For the 98%CR sample the strengthening from dislocations (generated during rolling) and from grain boundaries are the two dominant mechanisms; lattice defects (notably dislocations) act as barriers to further dislocation propagation and increase the yield strength, and the large dislocation population inhibits strain-hardening ability.

interfaces.interface_notes: Ordering strengthening operates by the splitting of dislocations into super-partial dislocations and creation of an antiphase boundary in the ordered phase (leading + trailing dislocation pair constraint), restricting dislocation mobility; this contribution is only a small cap for the 98%CR sample.
interfaces.phase_evolution: For the cold rolled (98%CR) condition the ordered phase and solid-solution strengthening are minor; upon recrystallisation (annealing) the dislocation and grain-boundary contributions decrease while ordering/solid-solution become dominant (not applicable to the as-cold-rolled state).

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Charges of interstitial free (IF) steel and pure aluminium were melted in a vacuum arc furnace to prepare low-density steels with 5, 6, 6.8 and 9 wt% Al; the obtained circular buttons (diameter 10 cm, height 5 cm) were re-melted 7-8 times to remove segregation.
The Fe-6.8Al alloy was cold rolled (CR) to 98% reduction in thickness from the as-cast state; this defines the 98%CR sample condition (state_label '98% CR').

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Uniaxial tensile tests on an Instron 5967 screw driven machine; three tensile tests conducted for each sample condition.
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: sub-size tensile specimen, gauge length 6 mm, width 2 mm; gauge section machined parallel to the rolling direction (RD)

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress-strain curve of the 98% CR sample rises almost vertically to a maximum just under 1800 MPa at ~2% strain, then falls steeply and terminates near 5% strain at ~1250 MPa.

phases_present.morphology: heavily elongated and pancaked grains along the rolling directions, containing shear bands at ~40 degrees to RD (non-uniform deformation)
nano-sized, very fine ordered phase (bright contrast in dark-field TEM) dispersed in the ferrite matrix

precipitates.distribution: very fine ordered particles dispersed in the ferrite matrix (dark-field TEM bright contrast, associated with dark background)

structures.overall_structure: Single-phase ferritic (BCC) matrix in the heavily deformed 98% cold rolled state: heavily elongated and pancaked grains along the rolling direction containing shear bands, together with a nanometre-scale Fe3Al ordered phase.

unmapped_findings: For the 98%CR Fe-6.8Al sample the yield ratio (YS/UTS) and the ultimate tensile strength are not reported ('-') in Table 4 (b0074); only YS = 1800 MPa and 1.2% uniform elongation are given.

The yield strength drop of the Fe-6.8Al alloy from 1800 MPa (98% CR) to 265 MPa (750 °C, 60 min anneal) is associated with the change in dislocation density from ~2.2 × 10^15 m^-2 (98%CR) to ~10^12 m^-2 (annealed), identifying dislocation strengthening as one of the main mechanisms (b0076).

Fig. 9 (figure_009) shows the stacked strengthening contributions for the 98%CR Fe-6.8Al bar (total YS = 1800 MPa): dislocations (magenta, roughly 900-1750 MPa) and grain boundary (blue, roughly 200-900 MPa) dominate, solid solution (black) is small (~200 MPa) and ordering (green) is only a thin cap.
The 98%CR sample's (110) XRD peak shows a large amount of broadening compared with the annealed samples, attributed to lattice micro-strain imparted during cold rolling (b0071).

The ordered-phase Mössbauer/SAXS characterizations were performed on filed powder samples annealed at 600 °C for 60 min (b0016), i.e. a sample-preparation state distinct from the 98%CR condition; ordered-phase sizes (TEM 2.1 ± 0.2 nm for Fe-6.8Al; SAXS 2.5-3.75 nm across 5-9 wt% Al) are therefore attributed to the Fe-6.8Al alloy rather than strictly to the as-cold-rolled state.
